facts.claim: Grace Hotel (Auberge Collection, Imerovigli) charges a flat venue fee. For celebrations over 50 people it includes exclusive use of the selected event spaces, tables and chairs for dining, lounge furniture and bars, glassware, china, silverware and napkins, event set-up and breakdown, event staffing, screens and room dividers, and transport between the hotel and the event site for guests staying overnight at Grace Hotel.

Grace Hotel: for weddings of 50 guests or fewer the flat venue fee includes exclusive use of the selected event spaces, tables and chairs for dining, glassware, china, silverware and napkins, a wedding arbour, event set-up and breakdown, and transport to and from the event site.

Grace Hotel's 'Furniture & Linens' note says custom tables, dining chairs, lounge furniture, glassware, china, silverware, white, navy or black napkins, set-up and breakdown, bartenders, event staffing and screens and room dividers are included in the facility fee.

Grace Hotel provides a dedicated event manager for venue details, but a wedding planner is required for all weddings and should be involved for a minimum of 3 months before the wedding; at the 363 Lounge the decor and seating are looked after by the couple's wedding coordinator.

Grace Hotel menus: for parties of up to 30 guests, offering an onsite choice of three pre-selected main courses is 'for a charge', with a minimum four-course menu; events over 30 guests may also select three main courses.

Grace Hotel accommodation: guests may book individually; for a room block or resort buyout the Sales Manager quotes on dates, rooms and room nights; the hotel does not require a minimum number of rooms. A DJ or live band is allowed (the hotel gives recommendations) and a private lounge with full-length mirror is available to the wedding party from 8am. Capacities: 363 Lounge 40 seated / 60 standing; The Villa 15 seated / 60 standing.

Canaves Collection (Oia) weddings page offers 'Wedding Package Options' via a downloadable wedding brochure; its enquiry form lists ceremony types Religious, Civil, Symbolic and Vow Renewal, and optional extras such as flower arch, gazebo, bouquets, wedding crowns, bombonieres, photographer, videographer, wedding cake, fireworks, 'Preparation of Wedding Documents', DJ, live bands, harpist and lighting (enquiry options, not stated package inclusions).

Canaves wedding brochure: the Panorama Balcony / Caldera Arches 'Wedding Ceremony & Dinner Reception for up to 30 guests' package (Canaves Oia Suites) includes private use of the ceremony and reception area for up to 5 hours (until 11:30pm), event planning services, recorded music of the couple's choice, a glass of sparkling wine for the toast, basic set-up (chairs, tables, white tablecloths, silverware), a two-tier wedding cake, and music up to 60 dB until 11:30pm. A room booking is not required but is recommended.

Canaves wedding brochure lists a Panorama Balcony 'Elopement for couple only' package with the same inclusions (5 hours private use until 11:30pm, event planning services, recorded music, sparkling wine toast, basic set-up, two-tier cake, music up to 60 dB). Caldera Arches dinner layouts: one long table for up to 25 or three tables for up to 30; the Panorama Balcony dinner reception is for up to 12.

Canaves wedding brochure: the Veranda (Canaves Sunday) ceremony and reception package for up to 40 guests includes private use for up to 5 hours (until 11pm), event planning services, recorded music, sparkling wine toast, basic set-up, two-tier cake and music up to 60 dB until 11pm. Room requirement: up to 20 guests must book two suites for at least three nights; 21 to 40 guests requires a buyout of Canaves Sunday under special terms.

Canaves wedding brochure, Canaves Epitome: Sunset Terrace package (couple only or up to 25 guests; up to 5 hours until 11pm, music up to 60 dB) requires one room for at least three nights for 8 to 25 guests; Sunset Terrace and Elements Restaurant (26 to 45 guests; 7 hours until 1am, music up to 70 dB) requires three rooms for three nights; Sunset Terrace, Pool Area and Elements (45 to 100 guests) requires four rooms (45-60), six rooms (60-80), a half buyout of 25 rooms (80-100) and a full buyout of 53 rooms above 100 guests, each with three-night minimums. All include event planning services, recorded music, sparkling wine toast, basic set-up and two-tier cake.

Canaves wedding brochure payment terms: a non-refundable deposit (stated as a percentage of the venue cost) secures the venue and starts planning; the balance is due one month before the event with the food and beverage cost; venue payments are always non-refundable and vendor cancellation fees follow each vendor's contract. Food and beverage menus are separate ('Explore our menus'). The brochure says weddings can be real or symbolic and an in-house wedding planner handles details.

Canaves Exclusives & Buyouts page: full-property buyouts of Canaves Epitome (53 rooms, max 170 guests), Canaves Oia Suites (48 rooms, 120), Canaves Ena (18 rooms, 45) and Canaves Sunday (10 rooms, 22), quoted through a 'Request Your Buyout Proposal' form; no buyout inclusions are published. Venue table: Epitome Outdoor Gardens theatre 180 / banquet 250 / reception 280; Omnia Pool Area 100/150/250; Sunset Terrace 100/80/100.

Katikies Hotels' events page lists 'Micro weddings' under 'Packages ideas' (small, exclusive ceremonies at its Santorini or Mykonos hotels) with no inclusions stated; the enquiry form's event types include Weddings and 'Hotel Take over'. Its events and concierge team says it plans and manages every detail of the wedding.

Katikies Santorini venues marked 'ideal for wedding ceremonies': Botrini's Restaurant at Katikies Santorini (60 seated / 100 standing); at Katikies Garden, Selene Restaurant (55 outside seated / 150 standing), St. Joseph Wine Cave (36 / 50) and Garden Pool Bar (36 / 100); at Katikies Chromata, Koukoumavlos Restaurant Deck (20 / 50), Katikies Lounge (20 / 30) and Chromata Pool Bar area (40-50 seated / 50 standing). The page also lists a customisable honeymoon package and a Celebrations offer with themed decorations and a sweet treat in the suite.

Grand Ambassador Santorini's venue page offers Wedding and Honeymoon Packages described as including champagne and strawberries on arrival, romantic candlelit dinners, couples' massages and bespoke details; couples may work with their own wedding planner or the hotel's concierge team. It lists over 700 sq m of outdoor space for up to 250 guests, a private photo session at a pool of the couple's choice (where available) and an optional private luxury transfer.

Kapari Natural Resort (Imerovigli) says it provides the couple's own dedicated wedding planner who, with the hotel team, handles the details; it helps plan and hold the ceremony and reception, accepts events for up to approximately 30 people, and also offers Honeymoon Packages (no inclusions listed).

Santorini Gem (caldera venue plus wedding villa) offers a downloadable 'Rental Packages 2026' brochure and says it can host large or smaller events in outdoor and indoor spaces with selected services and a variety of menus, plus wedding planning services. The home page publishes a promotional discount on the venue rental fee for new 2027 bookings (figure not recorded).

Santorini Gem Rental Packages 2026 lists a Ceremony Wedding Terrace Exclusive Hire (morning, event 10:30-11:30, bridal room from 10:15) with a white altar table, chandelier, lanterns, white Tiffany chairs, sound system, guest and accessible facilities and a bridal suite; a wooden gazebo with curtains is 'at an extra cost'; a per-extra-guest fee applies beyond the base group and children under 12 are complimentary. Prices are published in the PDF (not recorded).

Santorini Gem Rental Packages 2026: three Ceremony & Reception packages on the upper terrace and pool area (event 17:00-01:30): venue only; venue plus villa day use (12 noon to 01:30); venue plus villa overnight (12 noon to 10am next day). Included equipment: altar table, chandelier, lanterns with candles, white Tiffany chairs, sound system, round or rectangle tables, linen, plating, cutlery, accessible facilities, air-conditioned bridal room, in-house catering facilities and bar; gazebo 'at an extra cost'; an earlier start is charged per hour. Rental fees are published in euros (not recorded).

Santorini Gem villa hospitality (per Rental Packages 2026): 5 bedrooms sleeping 8, a welcome sparkling wine and seasonal fruit, mineral water, mini bar, linen, night security and breakfast for the couple and villa guests; breakfast for more friends is at additional cost. The villa page says five bedrooms for up to eight guests, four bathrooms, two living rooms, a private pool and gardens (bathroom count differs from the PDF's five).
facts.conflicts: Villa bathrooms: villa page says four, Rental Packages 2026 PDF says five.

facts.claim: Santorini Gem Venue Policy 2027-2028: all couples must have a wedding planner; the venue provides its standard set-up; set-up from 1pm on the day; no storage; the venue does not provide guest transport and guests must pre-book their own; music up to 80 dB, lowered to listening level at 11pm and off 15 minutes before the end time; bar closes 30 minutes before the end; confetti, plate smashing and flying lanterns not permitted.

Santorini Gem Venue Policy dining: Ceremony & Reception packages require choosing a set menu (20 adults minimum, 80 maximum) or a buffet (over 30 guests, poolside receptions buffet only); personalised menus may carry supplementary fees; set menus are starter, salad, main and dessert with wedding cake not included; open bar packages are optional but if chosen apply to all adults (and a children's open bar then applies); tips are not included in menu prices; no outside food or drink.

Santorini Gem Venue Policy booking terms: a non-refundable deposit of the rental fee secures the date, the rental balance is due 9 months before the wedding, and the food and beverage order must be final and paid 40 days before; a postponement handling fee applies and postponement is only to the following season; ceremony options on the booking form are 'Civil or Symbolic ceremony only', ceremony and reception, or ceremony, reception and villa overnight. Monetary figures and percentages are published (not recorded).
Santo Wines (Pyrgos) weddings page describes caldera sunset weddings and directs couples to its Event Manager by email, phone or request form; it publishes no package names, inclusions or conditions.

Venetsanos Winery's Wedding & Events page offers the Upper Terrace (250 sq m, caldera views) for ceremony, reception, private dinner or gala, maximum approximately 100 seated at round tables, 160 standing or 100 theatre style; costs and availability are given on request by email. No package inclusions are published.

Andronis 2026 wedding brochure 'Andronis Wedding Package' lists: preparation of the documents for the marriage licence, a marriage certificate issued in Greek, coordination and booking of the ceremony date and time with the Mayor (two witnesses required), floral decor for the ceremony, bridal bouquet and boutonniere, a two-tier wedding cake, a bottle of sparkling wine with chocolate-covered strawberries, a private cliffside ceremony area, Andronis Heart koufeta favours, a symbolic gift, and a romantic turndown with sparkling wine and strawberries.

Andronis brochure ceremony venues: Heart Pool and Grande Pool (Andronis Arcadia, Oia) and Lycabettus Restaurant cliff area (Andronis Luxury Suites, ceremonies 10:00-17:00, last at 16:00) each include two glasses of prosecco, koufeta and a jar of honey with walnuts, with prosecco for up to two additional guests charged separately. Receptions: Pacman Restaurant and Miltos' Greek Table offer full exclusivity or semi-private use by season; Lycabettus full exclusivity up to 40 guests and cliff area up to 20, with a curated degustation menu.

Andronis brochure a la carte services: concierge-assisted marriage registration at the Town Hall, round-trip Town Hall transfers, photography (1 hour, 50 images) and videography (2 hours, 3-7 minute edit), extra hours, hair and make-up, and musicians on request; officiant, florals, photography sessions, fireworks and other bespoke services 'can be arranged upon request at an additional charge'. Services also listed: wedding planner, flower decoration, photography and spa rituals.
Andronis Weddings & Celebrations page links the 2026 wedding brochure and an enquiry form (event types Wedding, Birthday, Anniversary, Dining Event).

Mystique, a Luxury Collection Hotel (Oia) says its wedding specialists take care of every aspect and help organise the wedding, its venues serve as the ceremony backdrop and the team will find the setting; it offers Elios Spa treatments and getting ready with the bridal party in a suite. No package names, inclusions or conditions are published.
Aroma Suites (Fira) has a Weddings page saying it hosts small ceremonies on its rooftop terrace above the caldera: elopements for two, vow renewals and celebrations of up to 15-20 guests.

Aroma Suites lists ceremony packages: Caldera Ceremonies on the rooftop terrace; an elopement package that 'includes the ceremony, a local photographer, flowers, and champagne on the rooftop terrace'; and sunset vow renewals with flowers, champagne and a photographer arranged.
Aroma Suites says it offers full planning support, handling 'florist, photographer, musician, legal paperwork' through local Santorini vendors it has used for years.

Aroma Suites describes three ways to marry there: (1) rent the rooftop terrace for the ceremony and the couple handles the rest; (2) buy out the whole hotel, with additional rooms at a nearby property arranged for larger groups and the reception on the terrace 'at extra cost'; (3) the hotel arranges details such as photographer, decor, flowers and catering, 'each at extra cost'.

Aroma Suites says pricing is tailored to date, group size and how much the hotel arranges; every wedding is a special request and couples contact the hotel with date and group size for prices and availability. No prices are published on the page.
Aroma Suites says ceremonies can be held at sunset, in the morning or after dark, and the couple can stay in its Honeymoon Suite the same night.

Kivotos Santorini's Luxury Weddings page says it hosts exclusive weddings and invites couples to combine the celebration with a hotel buyout for a villa-like experience with family and friends staying on site.

Kivotos Santorini's wedding enquiry form lists three named wedding packages, 'The Dreamy Life', 'The Live Life' and 'The Get Together' (plus 'Other'); the page does not describe what each package includes.

Vedema, a Luxury Collection Resort (Megalochori), states on its Marriott events page that it provides wedding services; ceremonies can be held at the resort, on the beach or elsewhere, with receptions at the Pool Restaurant or, for more privacy, the Canava Wine Bar; a private beach bonfire and barbecue are also offered.
Vedema's events page says its 400-year-old wine cellar can hold up to 120 guests for a banquet and 150 for a reception; its Thira Conference Center is listed at 75 (theatre).

Vedema's events page says a dedicated Celebration Consultant will arrange local support services, photographer and videographer, custom floral arrangements for the bride and venue, wedding cake and musical entertainment; optional arrangements include personalised menus and private dining, a horse-drawn carriage and fireworks.

Vedema's events page says the resort attends to 'all of the legal documents necessary to marry on Santorini' and can provide flowers, music or DJ, hairdresser, make-up artist, spa treatments, photographer and videographer and customised food and wine menus; its Elios Spa's two salon suites can be reserved together for the bridal party on the wedding day.

Vedema's events page publishes per-person catering prices for events (amounts not recorded here) and a separate Honeymoon Package that includes a complimentary candlelit dinner, a signature honeymoon amenity and flower bed decoration.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_302) says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most commonly with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages (a statement of no record of a previous marriage, a Single Status certificate or a No Record Result certificate); local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, a deceased spouse's death certificate, and your original birth certificate and passport. DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it also needs an authentication or apostille. It says each country decides what proof it accepts and there may be different regional and national laws. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_303) says you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if, when it took place, it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia. A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage but may not work as proof of a name change (check with your local registry of births, deaths and marriages), and Smartraveller suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm the certificate is valid in Australia. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says Australia does not recognise overseas marriages where one or both people are already married to someone else, not old enough to marry, too closely related, or forced to marry.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens (read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_304) lists among its notarial services witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI), witnessing notices of intended marriage, and legalisation of signatures and/or seals by authentication or apostille. An appointment is needed for all notarial services (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), though apostille and CNI documents can be submitted by post; apostilled documents and CNIs are available for collection within two working days unless same-day collection is arranged in advance, or can be returned by mail. The Embassy gives no legal advice, does not witness signatures on overseas documents, honorary consuls cannot provide notarial services, and a fee applies (amounts not recorded). The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice level for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (page updated 30 September 2026, shown as still current when read live 11 November 2026 UTC). It notes Greece is in an active seismic zone with earthquakes and volcanic activity, including near Santorini, and that wildfires occur in the extended summer period, June to September.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece advice says Greece is in the Schengen area; Australians can make short trips without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and on arrival for a short stay on an Australian passport you register fingerprints and a photo under the European Entry/Exit System (EES), which is free and needs no action before arrival, though it may cause delays at borders. Depending on why you are travelling and how long you stay you may need a visa, and entry conditions can change at short notice, so contact the nearest Greek embassy or consulate. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

Visit Greece lists flights from Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) to Santorini Airport with a travel duration of 50 minutes, and from Thessaloniki Airport (Macedonia) to Santorini Airport of 1 hour and 30 minutes (scheduled durations stated by the tourism board). The page as read gives no ferry route or crossing time from Piraeus.

The official website of Santorini Airport (JTR), served through Fraport Greece's airport systems, lists airlines serving the airport including Aegean Airlines, Olympic Air and Sky Express alongside European and Gulf carriers such as British Airways, Lufthansa, Qatar Airways, Etihad Airways, Gulf Air and FlyDubai, and has Schengen and non-Schengen departure areas. It lists ways to and from the airport by public bus and by taxi, and has an Accessible Travel section for passengers with reduced mobility.

The Hellenic National Meteorological Service (HNMS/EMY) 'Climatic Data by City' page has no Santorini (Thira) station; for the South Aegean it lists only Naxos and Rodos. Naxos is the nearest listed station and any figures must be labelled as Naxos, not Santorini.

HNMS Naxos station (lon 25.369, lat 37.081, altitude 3 m; the page states 'Data Period: None') shows monthly mean temperatures of 16.1 C in April, 19.6 C in May, 23.5 C in June, 25.1 C in July, 25.0 C in August, 23.0 C in September and 19.7 C in October. Mean maximum temperatures are 18.7, 22.1, 25.9, 27.1, 27.0, 25.1 and 21.9 C for the same months.

HNMS Naxos station shows monthly mean precipitation of 17.6 mm in April, 10.6 mm in May, 2.4 mm in June, 0.9 mm in July, 1.6 mm in August, 7.7 mm in September and 38.6 mm in October, with mean precipitation days of 6.0, 3.6, 1.1, 0.4, 0.3, 1.9 and 5.5 respectively.

HNMS Naxos station shows a prevailing wind direction of north in every month, with monthly mean wind power of 11.7 in April, 10.0 in May, 10.3 in June, 13.3 in July, 13.8 in August, 13.9 in September and 14.5 in October (units not stated on the page).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (level green); the page was updated 30 September 2026 and shows 'still current at 12 November 2026' when read on 11 November 2026 (Australian date).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says heatwaves are frequent over the summer months (drink plenty of water, wear light clothing, stay in air conditioning or shade, follow local authorities), and that wildfires occur during the extended summer period from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, prompting evacuations; fires can start with little warning and travel quickly. Expect travel disruptions in areas that might be affected.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's latest update says to be careful when swimming in Greece due to boat traffic, coastal hazards, strong currents and marine life, to check conditions and to swim at patrolled beaches where possible. It says lifeguards operate at many Greek beaches from June to September, sea conditions can change quickly, and to avoid swimming close to cliffs, rock faces or boats.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says during the May to October tourist season to be prepared for high temperatures and large crowds at popular seaports; in most cases you will carry luggage up and down stairs on ferries; ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly due to strong winds, so check the forecast and reconfirm departures. It says on some Greek islands, such as Santorini, smaller boats or tenders carry cruise ship passengers to and from shore and passengers using tenders may have difficulty with stairs.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says Greece is in an active seismic zone and experiences earthquakes and volcanic activity, and that Saharan dust storms occur, particularly in spring, reducing air quality and visibility.

Smartraveller (DFAT), 'How to get your documents legalised' (last updated 30/09/2026): ask the overseas authority which documents they need and which must be legalised; DFAT 'can't tell you what they may want'. Find out from the intended authority or legal representative whether you need an apostille or an authentication certificate.

Smartraveller: documents that are not original Australian public documents must first be notarised by an Australian Notary Public; the apostille or authentication certificate is applied directly to the document, so if you don't want originals marked, get a notarised copy legalised (and check the overseas authority accepts it).

insider_details.detail: At Canaves, the room-night minimum is part of the package: most Epitome and Sunday packages require booking rooms for at least three nights, scaling to a half or full buyout for larger groups, so compare quotes with accommodation included.

A 'venue fee' and a 'package' are different things: Grace Hotel's flat fee covers spaces, furniture, staffing and set-up but requires a separate wedding planner, while Andronis's package bundles paperwork, florals, cake and a ceremony area with services on top.

Food and drink usually sit outside the venue figure: Canaves takes food and beverage with the balance, and Santorini Gem requires a set or buffet menu choice, optional all-guest open bar, and a final F&B order 40 days out.
Check the music rules inside the package: Canaves packages cap music at 60 to 70 dB with fixed end times, and Santorini Gem lowers music at 11pm with a set close.
Guest transport is not a given: Grace Hotel includes event transport in its fee, but Santorini Gem states it provides no guest transport and guests must pre-book their own.

Small Fira boutique hotels can split the wedding into tiers: venue hire only, full buyout, or the hotel arranging suppliers, with each supplier charged on top; ask which tier a quote covers before comparing it with a resort package.
A named package is not a list of inclusions: Kivotos names three packages on its enquiry form but does not describe them, so request the written inclusions for the package named in any quote.

Capacity varies sharply by venue type: a Fira rooftop terrace suits up to 15-20 guests, while Vedema's wine cellar seats up to 120 for a banquet; match the guest list to the space before shortlisting.

Where a venue says it handles legal paperwork (Aroma, Vedema), confirm in writing exactly which documents it prepares and which the couple must obtain through the Municipality of Thira and the embassy.
